WHY THIS GATE EXISTS. The database and the edge functions build in-app links as string literals --
notification `link` columns, system-job `operator_route` values, and `search_workspace`, which
branches on role to send a platform admin to /admin/<kind>/<id>. Nothing verified those paths
exist. Three were broken: `search_workspace` emits eleven /admin/ prefixes and nine had a route,
so a platform admin searching a complaint number or a citation reference clicked the result and
landed on Not Found; and the integration webhook dispatch job's Open button pointed at
/admin/integrations, which has never been a route. No test noticed, because the link is assembled
in SQL and consumed as an opaque string -- GlobalSearch navigates `item.route` verbatim, with no
THE EXPECTED USE OF THIS FILE is a literal that a LATER migration supersedes. Migrations are
append-only history, so a path corrected by a later migration still appears in the original file,
and this check reads text rather than executing the schema -- it cannot tell that the row no
longer holds that value. An entry must name the superseding migration so the claim is checkable.

/admin/integrations.reason: Superseded. `20260711200651_phase2_signed_integration_hub.sql` seeded this as the `operator_route` of the `integration-webhook-dispatch` system job, and it has never been a declared route -- the System Jobs page renders operator_route as an Open button, so it went to Not Found. `20260805020000_an_operator_route_has_to_go_somewhere.sql` updates the row to `/admin/enterprise`, which is where the integration register, credential rotation and webhook endpoint controls actually live. The original literal remains in the older migration because migration history is append-only.
